title: Model update rollback & evidence playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working draft captures a lightweight operational + legal playbook for handling customer requests to roll back a model change (version rollback or config revert) and the associated evidence/e-discovery requests. Designed to be used by Security, Legal, SRE, and Customer Success during and after a model regression or sensitive-output incident.

Context / why we need this:
- Increasingly customers want a single canonical attachment for contract language that says how we will respond to requests for rollback and proof that their data / outputs were handled correctly.
- Existing templates cover DPA/retention but not the practical cross-team steps: what we preserve, how we snapshot KV/prefix caches, what logs to freeze, and SLAs for producing evidence.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — product/ops steps + legal checklist + sample clause to slot into customer exhibits.

Quick definitions used in this playbook:
- Model change: any change to model weights, tokenizer, decoding defaults, or runtime quantization profile that may affect outputs.
- Rollback request: customer asks Redwood to revert serving to a prior model version or configuration for their tenant/route.
- Evidence package: a time-bounded, tamper-evident set of artifacts produced for customer or legal review (snapshots, request IDs, sampling results, timelines).

Scope / Applicability:
- Applies to Hosted API customers and Dedicated deployments where Redwood controls runtime. For Private deployments we provide a slightly altered evidence checklist (operational-only, no access to customer premise artifacts).
- Not intended for training dataset provenance disputes — those follow Research/Policy track.

Trigger conditions (examples):
- Customer reports a regression following a canary rollout (quality/regulatory risk).
- Customer claims that specific PII was output and requests rollback + evidence of data handling.
- Legal/subpoena asks for timeline and snapshots around a model change.

High-level response timeline (target SLAs):
- Acknowledge request: within 4 business hours (CS/Legal triage).
- Initial safe action (if outage/safety): temporary route hold / redirect to previous model variant: within 1 hour for severity-critical incidents.
- Evidence package preliminary deliverable: 3 business days for small packages (<= 48h window), 10 business days for larger windows.
- Formal signed transfer / legal review may extend delivery.

Operational runbook (step-by-step):
1) Intake & classification (CS + Legal)
   - Create JIRA incident (tag: model-rollback-evidence) and assign to SRE + ML engineer + Legal liaison.
   - Collect customer-provided sample requests, approximate timestamps, tenant/route identifiers.

2) Immediate containment (if safety/regulatory risk):
   - Route policy: flip affected route to prior pinned model variant or route traffic to a staging fallback.
   - Flag the rollout ID in orchestration and prevent automatic re-rolls.
   - Communicate short note to customer: "we've pinned your route to previous model and are collecting evidence."

3) Forensic snapshot (SRE/ML engineer) — freeze artifacts and compute hash signatures
   - Snapshot serving config (model hash, config flags, quantization profile, kernel selection).
   - Export inference logs for the requested time window: request IDs, timestamps, route id, model version, token-level timing (if available).
   - Capture KV/prefix cache metadata: what entries exist, eviction metrics, TTLs. Do NOT include raw customer prompts unless required and approved by Legal.
   - Snapshot infrastructure state: pod/container images, GPU driver versions, runtime binary checksums.
   - Produce cryptographic checksums (sha256) for each artifact and store in internal evidence bucket with access controls.

4) Sample reconstruction & deterministic checks (ML engineer)
   - Attempt to deterministically reproduce reported outputs against the frozen model binary/config in an isolated environment. Note: streaming non-determinism may limit exact reproduction; document variance and RNG seeds if possible.
   - Run a targeted sample suite (customer-supplied plus additional edge cases) and record outputs and diffs.

5) Privacy review (Privacy/Security)
   - Review exports for PII. If raw prompts are present in snapshots, apply pseudonymization before sharing with external parties unless customer explicitly authorized raw export. Record pseudonymization mapping in internal audit only.
   - Document data minimization decisions (why specific artifacts were included/excluded).

6) Legal package assembly (Legal lead)
   - Assemble Evidence Package: README (what was collected), artifact manifest (filename, sha256, size, brief description), reproduction notes, and redaction checklist.
   - If customer requests chain-of-custody or notarized timestamps, coordinate with Compliance for time-stamping/attestation process.

7) Delivery & follow-up
   - Deliver preliminary package via secure transfer (S3 presigned link with TTL + Audit log) or as agreed under contract.
   - Offer a technical walkthrough session with ML engineer and SRE.
   - Agree retention/next steps: either close, escalate to remediation, or negotiate contractual remedies (credits/rollback commitments).

Minimum evidence checklist (artifact list to create):
- serving-config.json (model name, version hash, config flags)
- rollout-manifest.txt (rollout id, timestamps, operator id)
- inference-log.csv (request_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_version, timestamp, response_length, truncated boolean)
- sha256-manifest.txt (hashes for all artifacts)
- reproduction-report.md (deterministic reproduction attempts, seeds, diffs)
- kv-cache-metadata.json (counts, eviction stats; no raw cached entries unless approved)
- infra-snapshot.txt (container image, driver versions, kernel info)
- legal-readme.md (what's included, redactions, contact points)

Note on redaction & pseudonymization:
- Default: redact customer plaintext prompts in shared artifacts unless customer explicitly requests raw prompts and signs an authorization.
- Use deterministic pseudonymization mapping so internal reviewers can correlate entries but external recipients cannot re-identify. Keep mapping internal and time-limited.

Retention and archival:
- Evidence packages created for customer incidents are kept in a restricted evidence bucket for 90 days by default, extendable to 1 year on Legal request.
- After the retention window, artifacts are shredded per the vendor evidence deletion procedure and deletion logged.

Escalation matrix (contacts):
- CS lead: Leah Kim (pager-leah@redwood.com)
- SRE on-call: rotate (see SRE roster link in linked artifacts)
- ML engineer triage owner: Marco Ruiz
- Legal liaison: Jonah Meyers
- Privacy officer: Priya Singh

Sample contractual exhibit language (short form, to be adapted by Legal):
"Exhibit X — Model Change Rollback & Evidence Handling
If Customer reasonably demonstrates that a Model Change (as defined in the Agreement) materially caused a regression or disclosure of Customer Data, Provider will: (a) promptly, and where appropriate within one (1) hour, take interim mitigation steps (including reverting Customer traffic to the prior model variant); (b) produce an evidence package describing the artifacts retained, steps taken to reproduce the issue, and redactions applied; and (c) preserve a documented chain-of-custody for artifacts for a minimum of ninety (90) days. Provider's obligations under this Exhibit are subject to applicable law and Customer's execution of any necessary confidentiality and data handling authorizations.
Remedies are limited to those set forth in the Agreement and do not create new liabilities beyond the Agreement's caps and indemnities."

Open questions / TODO (team action items):
- Confirm whether we can automate sha256 generation and signed timestamping during rollout (Marco to prototype).
- Decide default retention length for evidence packages (Legal + Privacy to finalize).
- Add a short template e-mail for initial customer acknowledgement and another for final delivery (CS to draft).
- Integrate this playbook into the Console as a "Request evidence" workflow (product/console).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally short — looking for feedback on the reproduction expectations (how deterministic do we promise reproduction) and the retention period.
- Also want Legal input on whether the short-form exhibit creates any open-ended discovery risk.

Appendix: sample initial acknowledgement e-mail (CS)
Subject: Redwood — Acknowledgement of model rollback & evidence request
Hi [Customer Contact],
We received your request concerning model version [vX.Y] on route [route-id]. We have pinned your route to the prior model variant to reduce impact and have opened an internal incident (JIRA-ML-9876). Our team will assemble a preliminary evidence package and we will follow up with a delivery timeline within 72 business hours. If you are willing to provide raw input samples and a signed data-handling consent form, that will speed reproduction efforts.
Thanks,
[CS rep]

Appendix B: quick checklist for SRE snapshot command (example ops notes)
- capture-serving-config --route [route-id] --out serving-config.json
- export-inference-logs --from [ts] --to [ts] --filter-route [route-id] --out inference-log.csv
- dump-kv-metadata --route [route-id] --out kv-cache-metadata.json
- compute-sha256 --dir evidence/ --out sha256-manifest.txt

End of draft.

(Internal: do not publish externally until Legal approves final exhibit language.)
